chunks: And from him, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), similar to it —
and there is an addition in it: Muhammad ibn Ubayd said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! I do not have a wife.'
He (the Imam) said: 'Do you not have slave girls?' — or he said: 'Mothers of children?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Then you are not a bachelor.'

key_terms.أَعْزَب: Bachelor; one who is celibate or has no household intimate partner
key_terms.أَهْل: Wife or household; in this context refers specifically to a free wife
key_terms.أُمَّهَاتُ أَوْلَادٍ: Mothers of children (umm walad); slave women who bore children for their master, a recognized legal status
key_terms.جَوَارٍ: Slave girls (plural of jariya); female slaves in Islamic jurisprudence
key_terms.جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ: May I be sacrificed for you — a common devotional formula expressing deep respect and submission to an Imam

ai.seo_question: Does having a slave girl or mother of children count as not being a bachelor in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith is a continuation of the previous narration on the abhorrence of bachelorhood, transmitted through Abu al-Hasan (AS) with an additional exchange. When Muhammad ibn Ubayd — using the devotional formula 'may I be sacrificed for you' — claimed he had no wife (ahl), the Imam clarified that possessing slave girls (jawari) or mothers of children (ummahat awlad) also removes one from the status of being a bachelor (a'zab). The ruling reflects classical Islamic jurisprudence where intimate household relationships, including with slave women, were recognized as equivalent to marriage in terms of avoiding the spiritual harm of celibacy.

en.hubeali:
And from him, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Al Mugheira, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> similar to it, and there is an increase in it –
So Muhammad Bin Ubeyd said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! I do not have a wife for me’.
So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Is there no slave girl for you?’, or said, ‘Mother of the children?’ He said, ‘Yes’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So you are not with celibacy (not unmarried)’.
en.sarwar: 7. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from his father from ‘ Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah who has said the following: “‘Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah has narrated from abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, a similar Hadith
and added the following: Muhammad ibn ‘Ubayd said, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, I am not married.’

He (the Imam) asked, ‘Do you not have slave-girls’ or that he (the Imam) asked, ‘Do you not have mothers of your children?’ He replied, ‘Yes, I have.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘You then are not an unmarried man.’”
